title_clean: Why Technical Analysts Are Losing Money (and When Technical Analysis Works)
summary: Revisits his old 'technical analysis is bullshit' stance: TA itself is neither good nor bad - outcomes are dominated by capital context, position sizing and diversification. Two friends, same TA class, opposite results.
lessons: Never borrow money to trade and never hand money to someone else to trade for you.
Same signal, same class, opposite outcomes: capital context and sizing dominate the system.
Diversify within trading itself - allocate only a slice of capital to any one method.
When you size up after a loss, fear shrinks size; when you size small, reward cannot justify total capital.

title_clean: A Call Ratio Shared at a Conference - One-Year Review
summary: Reviews a long-dated call ratio shared publicly in late 2022: buy 16,000CE (Dec-2023), sell 2x20,000CE, sell 3x13,000PE as financing. Shows ~3,300-point cumulative profit (~1.65-1.7 lakh per set) with boring, low-stress management.
lessons: The money-making process should be boring, not exciting - slow positions beat daily thrill trades.
Financing a long-dated call with sold calls and puts turns a debit into near-zero-cost structure.
Have a mechanical exit rule - e.g. exit when VIX crosses 30 - before entering any position.
SEBI charges extra margin on option shorts expiring beyond nine months - price that into long-dated designs.

strategies.name: Long-dated call ratio (bullish, financing legs)
strategies.construction: Buy 1 lot 16,000CE Dec-2023 @~2,450; sell 2 lots 20,000CE @~700 each; sell 3 lots 13,000PE @~285 (later rolled to 15,000PE as market rose)
strategies.numbers: Net cost ~150 points after credits; ~15 months to expiry; result: 13,000PE ~+283 pts, 20,000CE ~+465 pts x2, 16,000CE ~+1,500 pts = ~3,300 pts (~1.65-1.7L per set); extra margin ~50k/lot for >9-month shorts
strategies.best_regime: Steady bull market with falling VIX; months of patience
strategies.adjustments: Roll sold puts higher as market rallies; scale out winners leg by leg
strategies.risks: Market below 13,000 breaks the put financing; above ~22,000 the short-call ratio turns against you; VIX spike forces exit

title_clean: I Was Wrong: Technical Analysis Is Not Bullshit - But...
summary: The full conversion story: a 2018 workshop dinner challenge introduced him to trend-following; changing one parameter (hourly to daily chart) made backtests work; two unrelated TA systems agree on trend. The real killer was position sizing, not the method.
lessons: The main job of technical analysis is identifying trend - different systems are different cars to the same destination.
One parameter change (hourly to daily timeframe) turned a failing system into a working one; test changes, not faith.
Nobody can tell you the 'right' position size - over-sizing turns one bad headline into account ruin, under-sizing makes wins meaningless.
Mix directional and non-directional allocations so no single regime can end your career.

strategies.name: Trend-following allocation mix
strategies.construction: Split capital ~4 ways: two non-directional (straddle-family) strategies + two directional (trend-following) strategies of different horizons
strategies.best_regime: All regimes - the mix, not the signal, is the risk control
strategies.adjustments: Rebalance emphasis as directional trends pay or non-directional premiums pay
strategies.risks: Directional books suffer in violent news-driven reversals; non-directional suffers in sustained trends

title_clean: Value vs Momentum Investing: Pros, Cons and How to Choose
summary: Contrasts momentum investing (entry and exit both matter, technicals time it) with value/contrarian investing (only entry matters; buy disasters, wait years). Documents his contra picks - ITC, PFC, REC, BSE - and a staggered crash-buying ladder.
lessons: Momentum: entry AND exit matter; value: only entry matters - know which game you are playing.
Every 2-3 years a crisis gives value investors their entry: 2008, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2022.
A 10% dividend yield is a bank-FD-like floor that pays you to wait for re-rating.
Never start SIPs at all-time highs; stagger: invest 1/3 at -10%, 2/3 at -20%, all at -30%.

strategies.name: Staggered crash-buying ladder (investor)
strategies.construction: At Nifty -10% from high: deploy 1/3 of earmarked capital; at -20%: another 1/3; at -30%: remainder
strategies.numbers: Since 2008 only Lehman (2008) and COVID (2020) produced >30% drawdowns; typical corrections 10-20%
strategies.adjustments: None - it is a pre-committed ladder, not a forecast
strategies.risks: Requires patience and cash discipline; drawdown can overshoot the last rung

title_clean: Beware the Positive Black Swan: Risk Cuts Both Ways
summary: Nassim Taleb's black swan concept explained, then flipped: traders face upside black swans too ('white swans') - the 2009 election-day +20% and the 2019 corporate-tax-cut candle. Risk management skill, not direction, is the survival variable.
lessons: Traders carry two-sided tail risk; investors only downside - plan for the honey tank, not just the drainage tank.
Selling calls, buying puts, and shorting futures are all short exposure - an upside black swan hits all three.
Policy can be a positive black swan: the 2019 corporate tax cut ignited a violent short-covering rally.
Adjustment skill - not prediction - determines survival when tail events strike either way.

title_clean: Is Now the Right Time to Buy Stocks? Cycles, Valuations and Patience
summary: At all-time highs he sides with cautious professionals: PMS houses pausing inflows, pre-election populist-budget risk, and asset-class cyclicality (his 1996 Chennai flat: 10 flat years then 4x in two). Investors should wait for the crash ladder; traders can ride momentum.
lessons: Asset classes wildly outperform for a stretch, then go lacklustre for years - never extrapolate a hot phase.
India's valuation premium (~3x other EMs) means future returns start from a high base; temper expectations.
Futures rollover costs (~150-170 points/month, ~1,800/year) silently erase most index-long futures returns.
Professionals manufacture pessimism to accumulate and euphoria to exit - the builder-refund parable in market form.

title_clean: The Only Strategy That Works Now: A Term-Structure Put Calendar
summary: India VIX reads only ~1-month options, so June 2024's election-loaded IV was invisible in it: calls bid, puts sticky. His answer - a reversed deep-ITM put calendar (sell Feb 23,000PE, buy June 23,000PE for a net credit) that made ~25% on margin in ten sessions with defined risk.
lessons: India VIX is a one-month instrument - it cannot see IV built for events six months out; check the term structure yourself.
When far-month IV exceeds near-month IV, reverse the calendar: sell near, buy far.
Deep-ITM calendars behave like cheap hedges with tiny margin - ideal for event-loaded quarters.
Far-month event premium (June 2024 election) can make short-dated strangles bleed even as the market rises.

strategies.name: Reversed deep-ITM put calendar (bullish, event-premium harvest)
strategies.construction: Sell near-month (Feb) 23,000PE and buy far-month (Jun) 23,000PE, same strike, 1:1
strategies.numbers: Entry 1 Jan 2024: buy Jun @1,150 / sell Feb @1,154 = net credit ~4 pts; margin ~30-35k; by 12 Jan: +181 pts (~10k, ~25% ROI); max loss ~4-5k per lot
strategies.best_regime: Bullish view + far-month IV > near-month IV (e.g., big event inside far expiry)
strategies.adjustments: Exit on IV crush after the event or on trend confirmation; roll sell leg monthly if needed
strategies.risks: Deep-ITM liquidity (10-20 pt spreads); a crash hits both legs - June leg cushions but slippage on small capital can still be 10-15% of margin

Over 15 Dec-12 Jan, the June 20,000PE barely moved (~25 to ~23) while the 23,000/24,000CE rose 150-200 points - far-month strangle sellers were trapped
Nifty closed at 21,741 on 29 December 2023 (referenced as the strategy's baseline)

quotes: When the far month carries the event, do the calendar backwards: sell the near month, buy the far month.
